sharedBrief: Square head-and-shoulders painted dark fantasy portraits matching the title artwork: amber firelight, blue-violet cavern shadows, weathered tangible materials, readable large faces. Edge-to-edge artwork without text, borders or UI.

portraits.brief: Ancient skeletal keeper of the Heart, parchment-dry skin, faint violet eye embers, corroded black iron crown, ragged indigo cowl, tarnished bronze ornament and a grave-magic hand. Calm calculating menace in a cavernous stone hall.

Massive living goblin king, earthy olive-grey skin, flattened nose, pointed ears, short lower tusks, calculating eyes, battered hammered gold crown, dark iron armour, leather, plundered gold clasps and one fur shoulder. A grounded master of a hoard.

Ancient dwarven forge automaton, geometric black iron mask, heavy hammered plates, rivets, soot and weathered engraving. Narrow amber eye slits and the Heart crystal burning inside its ribbed chest furnace. Massive hammer at the edge; no flesh, crown or futuristic technology.

lich.prompt: Create ONE finished square painted BESTIARY ENTRY illustration for Deepdelve. The first TWO images are the authoritative bestiary style and composition references; match them closely. The THIRD image supplies only the keeper's identity, face/head design and identifying materials. This keeper belongs in the SAME CREATURE BESTIARY as the first two, with their hand-painted dark fantasy illustration, rich controlled fine brushwork, weathered tangible materials, amber dungeon light from left, deep blue-violet shadow, old stone arches and cave atmosphere. Show the creature's HEAD AND UPPER BODY DOWN TO WAIST with characteristic arms/gear and a real sense of its dungeon habitat, as the reference creature entries do. Head occupies about a THIRD of square width, face readable; full head/crown and identifying gear inside the square with 5% breathing room. Species silhouette, outfit and characteristic role are more important than an isolated facial close-up. Recompose the third image into a creature illustration. Avoid the third image's tight hero-selection bust crop, repeated identical portrait backdrop, photographic pore-sharpening and character-card lighting. The first two bestiary references define the final brushwork and composition. Exactly one main subject, anatomically coherent, no extra limbs, no detached weapon pieces, grips physically meet shafts, joints continuous. Full-bleed opaque square 1024x1024 or largest available. NO text, captions, borders, UI, grids or watermark. SUBJECT: Dread Lich, ancient undead human sorcerer, dry skeletal skull, hollow nose, cold violet eyes, irregular antique-gold crown around a frayed black-purple hood, dark layered robes with restrained old gold/bronze trim. Same identifiable keeper as third reference. Lean upper body and both arms in the lower half, commanding a violet spell inside an ancient torchlit crypt. One skeletal hand extends palm up at chest height, tiny violet wisps hovering above it; four long fingers and one thumb with natural knuckles, wrist visibly attached to a continuous robed forearm. Other arm rests naturally against the body within the robe. No new staff or sword, no floating detached hand, no horns, no fleshy human face. Crown fully inside frame. Subject and habitat visually belong beside the bestiary's Dark Acolyte and Hollow Abbess. Keep dark hood, crown and cold magic as the identity, not a hero's shoulder-hilt pose.
